name: Vostok 2
first: First day in space — 17 orbits over 25 hours
description: Gherman Titov's 17-orbit, 25-hour flight — the second human in space and the first to spend over a day in orbit. Launched 1961-08-06 06:00 UTC from Baikonur; at 25 years 10 months Titov remained the youngest person ever launched into space until 2021 (Oliver Daemen, NS-16). Tested human reactions to prolonged microgravity — Titov reported the first case of space motion sickness, slept ~8 hours on orbit, and made the first hand-camera Earth photographs. Capsule landed near Krasny Kut, Saratov Oblast 1961-08-07 07:18 UTC after Titov ejected during descent. Service-module strap separation problem (same as Vostok 1) recurred.

events.label: EARTH PHOTOS
events.note: Titov made the first hand-camera photographs of Earth from orbit.

events.label: SLEEP
events.note: First sleep period in space (~8 hours).

events.label: EJECT + LAND
events.note: Capsule de-orbited; Titov ejected at ~7 km and parachuted to Krasny Kut.
